title: Adaptive priming curriculum and cost-aware sampler
author: Anika Rao
body:
Overview
========

This document describes the Adaptive Priming Curriculum and Cost-Aware Sampler (APCCS): a lightweight, production-grade pattern for generating, scheduling and labeling prompt probes that balance evaluation fidelity, token cost, and multi-tenant fairness. APCCS is intended for the prompt-sets-and-benchmarks and eval-harness teams as a standard for long-running sampling experiments and continuous drift detection in environments with mixed SLOs (latency-sensitive routes and budget-constrained routes).

Goals
-----
- Provide a repeatable curriculum model for priming templates and few-shot exemplars that adapts to workload drift.
- Prioritize sampling to meet token-budget targets while preserving statistical power for important slices.
- Offer tenant-aware weighting so small customers and enterprise accounts are not underrepresented.
- Integrate quantization-compatibility checks (fast lightweight probes) before committing high-cost annotation passes.

Non-goals
---------
- This is not a replacement for full shadow-eval. APCCS is an operational sampling and triage layer that feeds into the eval-harness.
- It does not replace safety cert pipelines or privacy-budgeted probes; those remain separate and gated.

Definitions
-----------
- Probe: A single prompt + metadata instance executed against a model variant.
- Curriculum: Ordered families of priming templates, from low-cost smoke checks -> medium-cost coverage probes -> high-cost annotated probes.
- Cost bucket: A label (smoke / normal / heavy) used to budget probe generation and annotation.
- Slice: A group of probes defined by attribute (language, tenant tier, prompt-class).

High-level design
-----------------
APCCS consists of four services (logical):

1) Sampler Service (daemon)
- Responsible for selecting probes from the catalog according to curriculum policy and per-slice budget weights.
- Exposes a /next-batch endpoint for the evaluator and a /report endpoint for probe outcomes.

2) Curriculum Manager
- Stores priming templates, exemplar families and TTLs. Provides staged promotion rules (smoke -> coverage -> annotation).
- Versioned and auditable. Curriculum artifacts are YAML manifests checked into the prompt registry.

3) Cost Estimator
- Real-time token cost estimator that uses current token-price table and expected sequence length distribution per template.
- Returns per-batch estimated cost and a confidence band.

4) Tenant Profiler
- Maintains tenant weights, last-sampled time, and fairness multipliers. Rules: enterprise_min_coverage and tail_tenant_boost.

Sampler algorithm (summary)
--------------------------
1. Query active curriculum for eligible templates and their priority weights.
2. Request estimated per-probe cost from Cost Estimator.
3. Apply tenant weights and slice importance adjustments.
4. Optimize selection to maximize slice-coverage subject to cost budget and expected latency (SLO) constraints.
5. Emit batch and log selection decisions for explainability.

Pseudocode
----------
```
# inputs: budget, latency_slo_ms, active_templates, tenant_weights
candidate_set = expand(active_templates)
costs = estimate_costs(candidate_set)
scored = []
for p in candidate_set:
  score = slice_priority(p.slice) * tenant_weights[p.tenant] / (1 + costs[p])
  scored.append((p, score))
selected = knapsack_maximize(scored, budget, latency_slo_ms)
return selected
```

Curriculum manifest example (YAML)
---------------------------------
```
name: entity-redaction-curriculum
version: v1.2
stages:
  - id: smoke
    templates: ["redact-smoke-01", "redact-smoke-02"]
    cost_bucket: smoke
    max_token_est: 150
    ttl_days: 7
  - id: coverage
    templates: ["redact-coverage-01", "redact-coverage-02"]
    cost_bucket: normal
    max_token_est: 400
    ttl_days: 30
  - id: annotated
    templates: ["redact-annot-01"]
    cost_bucket: heavy
    requires_annotation_review: true
```

Scheduling policies
-------------------
- Continuous sampling windows: default 24/7 low-priority; spike windows (business hours) for high-SLA tenants.
- Burst credits: each slice has a burst budget to handle ephemeral traffic surges without overrunning bucket.
- Probe TTL: a probe is re-eligible for re-sampling after TTL expires (configurable per-stage).

Config table: key thresholds and defaults
---------------------------------------
| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| daily_token_budget_per_project | 100000 | Hard token budget used by sampler per project/day |
| enterprise_min_coverage_pct | 5% | Minimum fraction of daily samples reserved for enterprise tenants |
| smoke_token_pct | 10% | Percent of budget reserved for smoke-stage probes |
| sample_batch_size | 128 | Default number of probes returned per /next-batch request |
| latency_slo_ms | 200 | Maximum acceptable model-response time for a candidate to be included in low-latency routes |

Operational runbook: creating and running a new curriculum
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Author YAML manifest and push to prompt-registry branch: refs/prompts/curricula/<name>.
2. Create a PR with: intent, expected token-cost, target slices and acceptance criteria. Assign Curriculum Manager reviewers.
3. Once approved, increment curriculum version and deploy to staging.
4. Run smoke-stage for 48 hours with smoke_token_pct=20% and observe: token spend, slice coverage, latency distribution.
5. If smoke checks pass, promote coverage stage for 7 days with limited annotation (5% of heavy probes).
6. If coverage passes, promote annotated stage and open annotation job with the annotation team.

Rollback and emergency stop
--------------------------
- Emergency stop: /sampler/admin/stop-all will immediately drain the sampler and cancel pending annotation jobs. Owner: oncall-eval (pager).
- Soft rollback: switch curriculum -> smoke-only and reduce daily_token_budget_per_project by 80%.

Telemetry and alerting
---------------------
Primary metrics to emit (aligns with eval-harness):
- sampler.probes.selected_per_minute
- sampler.token.estimated_spend_last_24h
- sampler.slice.coverage_percentile_{p50,p90,p99}
- sampler.latency.predicted_violation_count
- sampler.annotation.queue_depth
- sampler.selection.explainability_logs (sampled)

Alerts (examples)
- token_budget_burn_rate > 120% for 1 hour -> P1 to growth-owner and eval-oncall
- enterprise_min_coverage_pct < configured threshold -> P2 to customer-success and product
- annotation.job_failure_rate > 2% -> P1 to annotation-ops

Annotation economics and costing guidance
---------------------------------------
- Cost buckets: smoke (cheap, automated), normal (minimal human review), heavy (full annotation).
- Example per-unit costs (internal benchmark, USD):
| bucket | model_cost_per_probe | annotation_cost | total_estimated |
| smoke | $0.002 | $0 | $0.002 |
| normal | $0.01 | $0.05 | $0.06 |
| heavy | $0.03 | $0.25 | $0.28 |
- Budgeting guidance: cap heavy bucket to 2–5% of total daily probes unless explicitly approved.

Quantization and compatibility checks
------------------------------------
- For each curriculum stage, mark templates as quant-safe or quant-sensitive. The sampler must run a lightweight quant-check run (fast_prompt variant) against the quantized artifact prior to gating annotation.
- If quant-check fails (coherence delta > configured threshold), tag the probe for fallback to float baseline and notify model-onboarding.

Fairness and multi-tenant considerations
--------------------------------------
- Tenants are stratified into Tiers (free, standard, enterprise). By default the sampler applies a fairness floor: ensure free-tier tenants have at least 1% daily representation unless they opt-out.
- Tail-tenant boost: small tenants with historical low sampling get an automatic boost multiplier capped at 3x for the first 14 days after signup to gather coverage.

Acceptance criteria for curriculum promotion
-----------------------------------------
- Smoke pass: <1% unexpected failure rate, token burn within 15% of estimate, p95 latency within configured bound.
- Coverage pass: coverage across priority slices >= target (config in manifest), annotation pass rate <= 8% disagreement.
- Annotated pass: annotation inter-annotator agreement (IAA) >= 0.75 on critical slices; regression-safety checks green for last 3 days.

Ownership, review cadence and lifecycle
-------------------------------------
- Owner: applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-stewards (primary).
- Reviewers: eval-harness, model-onboarding, privacy, annotation-ops.
- Cadence: curriculum artifacts reviewed quarterly and after any model-version change affecting tokenization/sequence-length.

Appendix A: example CLI (sampler admin)
--------------------------------------
# list active curricula
redwood-sampler-cli list-curricula --env=staging

# run a one-off batch for a tenant with cost cap
redwood-sampler-cli one-off --curriculum entity-redaction-curriculum --tenant=acme-corp --max-tokens=1000

# emergency stop
redwood-sampler-cli admin stop-all --reason=\"latency spike detected\"

Appendix B: quick troubleshooting checklist
------------------------------------------
- If token burn is unexpectedly high: review cost estimator logs, check for template change that increased seq length.
- If slice undercoverage: check tenant weights and recent tenant signups; ensure fairness floor not disabled.
- If quant-check failures spike: isolate the quant artifact and run replay-suite from runtime-fingerprint-onboarding.

Related artifacts and references
--------------------------------
- Curriculum manifests live in refs/prompts/curricula/ on the prompt-registry repo.
- See eval-harness/probe-scheduling-fairness docs for knapsack solver details.
- Link to annotation-ops cost schedule (internal): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/annotation-cost-schedule
